evidence: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:38-42 — the second OR branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` has no method filter, so as written it matches any WorkflowReminder. But today it can't hit non-SMS rows: grep shows retryCount is only incremented at scheduleSMSReminders.ts:184 and :195, on rows fetched with method SMS (:50). Every other row keeps the default of 0 (schema.prisma:1000, migration DEFAULT 0). So nothing breaks now, but this is a real latent hazard. If WhatsApp or email retry logic later reuses the column, the SMS cron would delete those rows. Adding `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` to the second branch is a cheap guard that makes the intent explicit.

scheduleSMSReminders.ts:158 — if the message is empty or sendTo is missing, no retryCount update happens; the increments are only in the else branch at :178-186 and the catch at :189-197. The claim that these rows are processed 'indefinitely' is wrong. The first deleteMany branch (:32-37) removes SMS reminders once scheduledDate <= now, so each row is re-processed for at most the 7-day window (:52-54). This is also the behaviour before the PR. Still, a missing sendTo or message is a permanent failure, so counting it as a retry would match the PR's goal and stop pointless per-run work (e.g. the prisma.profile query at :111). Worth doing as a small improvement, not a bug.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleWhatsappReminders.ts:22-41 — the WhatsApp cron has no retryCount handling; its deleteMany only filters on method WHATSAPP plus scheduledDate. So the inconsistency is real. However, the PR is explicitly scoped to SMS (title and description), and failed WhatsApp reminders are still bounded by the scheduledDate deletion rather than retried forever. Extending the same logic to WhatsApp is a reasonable follow-up, not a defect in this PR. If it is done, issue 0's method filter becomes necessary.

scheduleSMSReminders.ts:68-70 — the `continue` when workflowStep or booking is null skips the retryCount increment. This check predates the PR. The 'indefinitely' claim is wrong: the deleteMany at :32-37 removes these SMS rows once scheduledDate passes. Both relations are optional (schema.prisma:990, :996), and skipping costs no DB or Twilio calls, so the extra work per cron run is negligible. Incrementing retryCount here would just delete them a few days early. No change needed for this PR.
